reasoning: March 2025 set a record low for March with 14.1 million km². The question asks if March 2026 will be even lower. Arctic sea ice has declined at ~2.5% per decade, but year-to-year variability is substantial. While the long-term trend is downward, breaking a record set just one year prior is challenging. Natural variability, atmospheric patterns, and ocean conditions can cause significant fluctuations. The probability of a new record low in consecutive years is relatively low, though not negligible given the accelerating decline trend.
